Ui.Script:
-- Step the bar one row (the slider's valueStep) — the sensible step for an item list (the -- generic ref scrollbar steps half its height; a discrete row list wants one). Silent by -- design: the ref plays UChatScrollButton only on the arrow *buttons'* OnClick, never on the -- wheel (ScrollFrameTemplate_OnMouseWheel is soundless). Both the wheel and the arrows call -- this, so the click lives on the arrow OnClick, keeping wheel-scroll silent. function BenillaScrollBar_Step(scrollBar, dir) local step = scrollBar:GetValueStep() if step <= 0 then step = 1 end scrollBar:SetValue(scrollBar:GetValue() + dir * step) end
-- Grey the up arrow at the top and the down arrow at the bottom (ref -- ScrollFrame_OnScrollRangeChanged's arrow handling), from the slider's own value/range. function BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(scrollBar) local minV, maxV = scrollBar:GetMinMaxValues() local val = scrollBar:GetValue() local up = getglobal(scrollBar:GetName() .. "ScrollUpButton") local down = getglobal(scrollBar:GetName() .. "ScrollDownButton") if val <= minV then up:Disable() else up:Enable() end if val >= maxV then down:Disable() else down:Enable() end end
-- The scrollbar's OnValueChanged: derive the row offset from the (pixel) value and, only when -- it actually moved, repaint the owner's list. The change-gate is load-bearing: the owner's -- repaint calls _Update below, which SetValue()s the thumb back to offset*itemHeight — a value -- that maps to the SAME offset, so this handler no-ops and the cycle stops after one hop (the -- Slider's own SetValue change-gate stops the value side, decision 0250). function BenillaFauxScrollBar_OnValueChanged(scrollBar, value) local frame = scrollBar:GetParent() local step = scrollBar:GetValueStep() if step <= 0 then step = 1 end local newOffset = floor(value / step + 0.5) if newOffset ~= frame.offset then frame.offset = newOffset if frame.updateFunc then frame.updateFunc() end end BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(scrollBar) end
-- OnLoad: a fresh faux frame is at the top with an empty range (ref ScrollFrame_OnLoad). function BenillaFauxScrollFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame.offset = 0 local scrollBar = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "ScrollBar") scrollBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, 0) scrollBar:SetValueStep(1) scrollBar:SetValue(0) end
-- The offset getters/setters the owner's list code reads (ref FauxScrollFrame_GetOffset / -- _SetOffset). _SetOffset syncs the thumb too, so a programmatic reset (top-of-list on open) -- moves the bar. function BenillaFauxScrollFrame_GetOffset(frame) return frame.offset or 0 end
function BenillaFauxScrollFrame_SetOffset(frame, offset) frame.offset = offset local scrollBar = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "ScrollBar") scrollBar:SetValue(offset * scrollBar:GetValueStep()) end
-- Seat a trough ON ITS BAR. THE SOCKETS, and why this is not a free choice: the channel art -- is not a plain tube — each end carries a 16-tall SOCKET that the arrow button drops into, -- bounded by the frame's outer cap and an inner crossbar. Measured texel-exact off -- UI-Character-ScrollBar (64x256): -- top piece (left column) : rows 0-3 CAP · rows 4-19 SOCKET · rows 20-21 crossbar -- bottom piece (right column): rows 85-86 crossbar · rows 87-102 SOCKET · rows 104-106 CAP -- Both pieces draw 1:1 anchored to their own end of the trough, and the arrow buttons sit 16 -- outside the slider's ends — so a socket lands on its arrow only when the trough OVERHANGS -- the bar by 21 above and 20 below (4 rows of cap at the top against 3+1 at the bottom; that -- 1 is the whole asymmetry). Those are the ref's own numbers, reached from the other side: -- ReputationFrame hangs its trough at the scroll frame's TOPRIGHT (-2,+5) / BOTTOMRIGHT -- (-2,-4) against a bar seated (6,-16)/(6,+16) — 21, 20, and the 8-left hang -- (ref-ReputationFrame.xml l.573-599 against ref-UIPanelTemplates.xml l.166-181). Miss it by -- even 4 and the arrows ride OUT of their sockets onto the caps with a sliver of bare socket -- showing beside them, which is exactly what B224 reported. -- -- Seated HERE, off the bar, rather than restated in each owner's XML: it is one law, and an -- owner made to re-derive it in offsets is an owner that can get it wrong — which is how -- B224 happened. So a trough carries NO anchors of its own; declare it before the bar (so it -- draws beneath) and name it `<barname>Trough`, and that is the whole contract. Lazy, -- because the bar is declared after the trough and does not exist at the trough's OnLoad. function BenillaScrollTrough_Seat(trough, scrollBar) if trough.seated then return end trough.seated = true trough:ClearAllPoints() trough:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", scrollBar, "TOPLEFT", -8, 21) trough:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", scrollBar, "BOTTOMRIGHT", 7, -20) end
-- Show/hide a bar TOGETHER WITH ITS TROUGH — the recessed channel it rides in, if the -- owner authored one beside it (a `<barname>Trough` frame on BenillaScrollTroughTemplate -- below). Every path that shows or hides a bar goes through here, so a window that fits -- shows neither and one that overflows shows both — and so a trough is seated on its bar -- before it can ever be visible, whichever way the first call goes. -- -- Why the trough is OPT-IN rather than part of the bar template: 1.12 authors trough art -- PER WINDOW, never in the shared scroll kit — `UIPanelScrollBarTemplate` carries only the -- two arrow buttons and the knob, and the ref's FrameXML then hangs loose trough textures -- beside 29 individual bars, in two different skins (UI-Character-ScrollBar for the -- dialog/paperdoll family, UI-ClassTrainer-ScrollBar for the trainer family). The era's own -- MinimalScrollBar went the other way and made its Track part of the bar; this pair keeps -- the era's COUPLING (track lives and dies with the bar) on 1.12's per-window SKIN. function BenillaScrollBar_SetShown(scrollBar, shown) local trough = getglobal(scrollBar:GetName() .. "Trough") if trough then BenillaScrollTrough_Seat(trough, scrollBar) end if shown then scrollBar:Show() if trough then trough:Show() end else scrollBar:Hide() if trough then trough:Hide() end end end
-- Reconcile the bar to a freshly-sized list (ref FauxScrollFrame_Update): clamp the offset into -- range, set the pixel range + step, seat the thumb at the current offset, and show the bar only -- when the list overflows the visible rows. Called by the owner's list-repaint each pass. function BenillaFauxScrollFrame_Update(frame, numItems, numToDisplay, itemHeight) local scrollBar = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "ScrollBar") local maxOffset = numItems - numToDisplay if maxOffset < 0 then maxOffset = 0 end if not frame.offset or frame.offset > maxOffset then frame.offset = maxOffset end if frame.offset < 0 then frame.offset = 0 end
scrollBar:SetValueStep(itemHeight) scrollBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, maxOffset * itemHeight) scrollBar:SetValue(frame.offset * itemHeight) BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(scrollBar)
BenillaScrollBar_SetShown(scrollBar, numItems > numToDisplay) end
-- A wheel spin over the list → one row (WoW convention: +1 up, −1 down). Called from the -- owner window's OnMouseWheel (the engine bubbles the spin up the parent chain, so the handler -- lives on the window, not a child — TrainerFrame.xml's own note). function BenillaFauxScrollFrame_OnMouseWheel(frame, delta) local scrollBar = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "ScrollBar") BenillaScrollBar_Step(scrollBar, -delta) end
-- ══════════════════════════ The REAL-scroll kit ══════════════════════════════════════════ -- -- The other half of the file: a true `<ScrollFrame>` (engine mechanism, decision 0112) that -- pans and CLIPS a variable-height child, as against the faux kit above (fixed rows re-bound -- to a data offset). Windows whose content height is unknown until it is laid out — a gossip -- menu of wrapped options, a quest's body text — need this one; a uniform list wants the faux. -- -- SHAPE, from the reference `UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate` (Interface\FrameXML\ -- UIPanelTemplates.xml l.166-211, extracted via mpqx): the scrollbar is a SLIDER that rides -- its ScrollFrame as a child, so `bar:GetParent()` IS the frame it scrolls — no name -- derivation, and `$parentBar` gives SyncBar its handle. The ref's OnVerticalScroll drives -- the bar's value and greys the two arrows at the ends; ours does the same through the -- shared arrow helper above. BENILLA_SCROLL_STEP = 20 -- px per arrow click / wheel notch BENILLA_SCROLL_PAD = 20 -- breathing room under the last element in the child
-- The bar moved (drag, arrow, or SyncBar): pan the frame it rides. The loop this could form -- (bar → scroll → OnVerticalScroll → SyncBar → bar) dead-ends in one hop — SyncBar writes the -- value the bar already holds, and the Slider's SetValue change-gate (decision 0250) drops it. function BenillaScrollBar_OnValueChanged(bar, value) bar:GetParent():SetVerticalScroll(value) BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(bar) end
-- Reconcile a ScrollFrame's bar to its live range (ref ScrollFrame_OnScrollRangeChanged): -- the bar spans [0, range] in pixels, seats at the current scroll, and hides entirely when -- the content fits. Wired to both OnScrollRangeChanged and OnVerticalScroll by the owner. function BenillaScroll_SyncBar(sf) local bar = getglobal(sf:GetName() .. "Bar") if not bar then return end local range = sf:GetVerticalScrollRange() bar:SetValueStep(BENILLA_SCROLL_STEP) bar:SetMinMaxValues(0, range) bar:SetValue(sf:GetVerticalScroll()) BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(bar) BenillaScrollBar_SetShown(bar, range > 0) end
-- Pan by `delta` px; the engine clamps to [0, range]. function BenillaScroll_Step(sf, delta) sf:SetVerticalScroll(sf:GetVerticalScroll() + delta) BenillaScroll_SyncBar(sf) end
-- WoW wheel convention: +1 per notch up, -1 down — up lifts the content. function BenillaScroll_OnMouseWheel(sf, delta) BenillaScroll_Step(sf, -delta * BENILLA_SCROLL_STEP) end
-- A widget's resolved bottom edge for the content sum — nil when it isn't contributing -- (hidden frame / blank FontString / not yet resolved this frame). function BenillaScroll_WidgetBottom(w) if not w then return nil end if w.IsShown then if not w:IsShown() then return nil end elseif w.GetText then local t = w:GetText() if not t or t == "" then return nil end end return w:GetBottom() end
-- Size a scroll child to its MEASURED content — the resolved bottom of the lowest visible -- widget, plus padding — instead of a fixed budget, and tell the frame (which fires -- OnScrollRangeChanged → the owner's SyncBar). Frame-late by nature: rects resolve after Lua -- runs, so owners re-run this from an OnUpdate until it stops changing. Returns true when it -- actually resized (only a real change writes: SetHeight invalidates layout, and an -- every-frame write would fight the resolver). function BenillaScroll_ResizeChild(scrollName, widgets) local sf = getglobal(scrollName) local child = getglobal(scrollName .. "Child") local top = child:GetTop() if not top then return false end local bottom = nil for i = 1, table.getn(widgets) do local b = BenillaScroll_WidgetBottom(getglobal(widgets[i])) if b and (not bottom or b < bottom) then bottom = b end end local height = 1 if bottom then height = (top - bottom) + BENILLA_SCROLL_PAD end if height < 1 then height = 1 end if math.abs(child:GetHeight() - height) < 1 then return false end child:SetHeight(height) sf:UpdateScrollChildRect() return true end
